# ciphertrust_user (Resource)



## Example Usage

```terraform
# Terraform Configuration for CipherTrust Provider

# This configuration demonstrates the creation of a user resource
# with the CipherTrust provider, including setting up user details.

terraform {
  # Define the required providers for the configuration
  required_providers {
    # CipherTrust provider for managing CipherTrust resources
    ciphertrust = {
      # The source of the provider
      source = "ThalesGroup/CipherTrust"
      # Version of the provider to use
      version = "1.0.0-pre3"
    }
  }
}

# Configure the CipherTrust provider for authentication
provider "ciphertrust" {
	# The address of the CipherTrust appliance (replace with the actual address)
  address = "https://10.10.10.10"

  # Username for authenticating with the CipherTrust appliance
  username = "admin"

  # Password for authenticating with the CipherTrust appliance
  password = "ChangeMe101!"
}

# Add a resource of type CM User with the username frank
resource "ciphertrust_user" "sample_user" {
  # Full name of the user
  name="frank"
  # E-mail of the user
  email="frank@local"
  # The login name of the user
  username="frank"
  # The password used to secure the users account
  password="ChangeIt01!"
}

# Output the unique ID of the created User
output "user_id" {
	value = ciphertrust_user.sample_user.id
}

# Output the username
output "username" {
    value = ciphertrust_user.sample_user.username
}
```

## Immutable Fields

The following fields cannot be changed after resource creation. Attempting to change them in config produces an error at `terraform plan` time — no API call is made and no destroy+recreate occurs:

| Field | Reason |
|---|---|
| `username` | Enforced by `modifiers.ImmutableString()`. CM does not allow renaming users after creation. |
| `is_domain_user` | Enforced by `modifiers.ImmutableBool()`. Absent from the `PatchUser` request body schema for `PATCH /v1/usermgmt/users/{user_id}` per the CM swagger; CM does not accept this field in PATCH requests. |

## Drift Detection

**Out-of-band deletion**: If the user is deleted directly in CipherTrust Manager (outside of Terraform), the next `terraform plan` or `terraform refresh` calls `Read()`, which receives HTTP 404. The provider adds a warning and removes the resource from state (`RemoveResource`). The subsequent plan proposes re-creating the user.

**Attribute changes**: Mutable attributes (`email`, `name`, `nickname`, `user_metadata`, `prevent_ui_login`, `password_change_required`) are re-read from CM on every plan and refresh. Changes made out-of-band to these fields surface as a non-empty plan diff, prompting the user to re-apply.

## Notes

- `password` is write-only and Sensitive. CM does not return credentials in GET responses; the provider preserves the value from prior state on every refresh. If `password` is removed from config after the initial apply, the prior value is automatically preserved in the PATCH payload to prevent sending an empty password to CM.

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `password` (String, Sensitive) The user's password. Write-only — CM never returns this value. The provider preserves the prior state value on refresh and update.
- `username` (String) (Immutable) Username of the user. Cannot be changed after creation.

### Optional

- `email` (String)
- `is_domain_user` (Boolean) (Immutable) Set to true if user is a domain user. Absent from the CM PATCH schema; cannot be changed after creation. Removing this attribute from config after setting it to true also triggers the immutability error — destroy and recreate to change.
- `name` (String) Users full name
- `nickname` (String)
- `password_change_required` (Boolean)
- `prevent_ui_login` (Boolean)
- `user_metadata` (Map of String) Information that can be stored with the user.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The ID of this resource. Populated from the CM `user_id` field after create.
- `user_id` (String) The unique identifier assigned by CipherTrust Manager.
